items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: I can remember when they opened up the taverns, Roosevelt come in and oh yes -- there was a tavern right across the street from where

ctx.x: Oh, he would say, 'That was a mess.' See, Reverend Turner was a strange musical man, and he had his beliefs. Now on Saturday nights, his favorite music movie was the 8th Street Theatre -- to me, that was a forerunner of this Grand Old Opry. Every Saturday night when I wasn't out hustling with the various new groups, he'd say, 'Now that's the kind of music you should listen to.' And I got a whole lot of the old Hoosier Hotshots; that's another side of it -- the music was beautiful. We had bands coming from the…

Now I'm kind of getting ahead of myself - but there was just plenty of music around Chicago at the time in the thirties ... World's Fair; World's Fair of 1933 and World's Fair of 1934. I can remember when they opened up the taverns, Roosevelt come in and oh yes -- there was a tavern right across the street from where

we were living at the time -- 32nd and State. It would open up and one of the fellows come and got me, I guess because I was young and I could dance a little bit. We'd go in and one of them would play the piano. They had me tap dancing, they'd pass a hat, and if I made a quarter or a half dollar, I was doing good.
